name: Golden Noise (NPNet)
plain: Passes the Gaussian start noise and the prompt embedding through a small trained network that outputs a better starting noise. Pre-model, one forward pass and no sampler changes. The network was trained at a specific size and token length, so the code resizes noise to 128×128 and handles prompt length.
math:
te = text_embedding(ε, c) ; g = unet_embedding(ε + te).
ε' = unet_svd(ε) + (2·sigmoid(α)−1)·te + β·g. α, β learned.
ε is made at 128×128 (nearest-exact resize when different) and result resized back.

providers.note: Splits long prompts into 77-token chunks and applies recursively; local patch skips partial trailing chunk. Falls back to base noise on any exception.

providers.author: asagi4
providers.note: Separately written; offers resize or crop, several reshape methods, and truncate, average or recurse for long prompts.

label: from code
surprise: Nearest-exact resize to 128×128 and back is applied to noise tensors whenever the latent is another size, which duplicates or drops noise pixels (effect on images not tested here).
